about: Curated recent advances for the Supercon Progress app. Each entry needs a reference in refs (a DOI, or an https link for preprints and project pages). Entries are merged with the ones built into the app: an entry with the same ref replaces the built-in one, and refs listed in hide are removed. cards: the Theory & materials cards it belongs to (their animation ids, e.g. zr, mott, stripes, dwave, phase), or ai for the AI × superconductors view. kind: experiment, theory, computation or news. Texts are summaries in our own words.

recent.h: Bulk phonons and weak screening can make Fermi-arc surface superconductivity nodal
recent.x: A continuum theory of time-reversal-invariant Weyl semimetals shows that Fermi-arc surface electrons can pair through phonons, mostly bulk ones for PtBi₂-like parameters, while the bulk itself stays normal. Pairing within a single arc favours a nodeless gap, whereas pairing between the two disconnected arcs gives a gap that changes sign along the arc. When the surface screens Coulomb repulsion poorly, the nodeless channel is suppressed and only the sign-changing one survives, with nodes at the arc centres, in line with ARPES on PtBi₂, where arc superconductivity appears below about 14 K. The authors propose tuning the screening, for example with a surface coating or gating, to engineer the critical temperature and the size and symmetry of the gap.

recent.h: Twist-angle disorder can make a fully gapped moiré superconductor look nodal
recent.x: Elasticity theory shows that even a small density of random lattice defects leaves moiré graphene with twist-angle variations that are correlated over long distances, decaying only logarithmically. Modelling twisted bilayer graphene as a network of superconducting islands whose local Tc, up to about 4 K, follows the local twist angle, the authors find that the BKT jump in the superfluid stiffness smears into a percolative crossover and that a fully gapped s-wave state can show a roughly linear-in-T drop in stiffness at low temperature, the signature usually read as nodal pairing. They argue that existing stiffness data on twisted graphene should be re-examined, and propose the real part of the microwave conductivity, which keeps a residual at low temperature when correlated disorder matters, as a diagnostic.

recent.h: Circularly polarized terahertz light tells electron and hole vortex-core states apart in FeTe₁₋ₓSeₓ
recent.x: Terahertz Faraday-rotation spectroscopy on 40 nm FeTe₁₋ₓSeₓ films (x = 0.15 and 0.38, Tc about 13 K) resolves transitions between the Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon bound states inside vortex cores. Because electron-like and hole-like states absorb light of opposite circular polarization, the lifetime, vortex mass, coherence length and upper critical field of each band can be obtained separately. The fitted resonances lie at 0.36 THz for electrons and 0.99 THz for holes at x = 0.15 and at 0.89 and 0.72 THz at x = 0.38, while the electron-to-hole carrier ratio in the cores falls from about 4:1 to about 1:1. The analysis treats the two condensates as independent and leaves coupling between them to future work.

recent.h: Band quantum geometry selects Kekulé superconductivity in Haldane phases
recent.x: A theory of spin-polarized rhombohedral graphene in a Haldane phase finds that the quantum geometry of its bands favours pairing within each valley and selects a chiral Kekulé state: a pair-density wave modulated on the scale of the lattice. The authors suggest kagome metals as another place to look for it.

recent.h: Coherence length and penetration depth computed from first principles
recent.x: Superconducting density functional theory, extended to Cooper pairs with finite momentum, yields Tc, the coherence length and the London penetration depth without adjustable parameters for Al, In, Sn, Ta, Pb, Nb, V₃Si and compressed H₃S. For Nb it gives Tc = 8.1 K against 9.5 K measured and ξ₀ = 34 nm against about 39 nm; H₃S comes out at 181 K against 184 K. Every material is correctly classed as type I or type II; the largest relative error is for Al (1.6 K against 1.1 K).

recent.h: Two superconducting orders meet at a tetracritical point in UTe₂
recent.x: Ultrasound measurements under hydrostatic pressure up to about 1 GPa trace two superconducting transitions in UTe₂ whose lines cross near 0.2 GPa and 1.6 K, a tetracritical point. Below it the two orders coexist as one multicomponent state, and a similar state appears at ambient pressure between about 12 and 18 T with the field along the b axis. Whether the combined state breaks time-reversal symmetry is not established.

recent.h: Terahertz light reveals clean d-wave pairing in a samarium nickelate
recent.x: Ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy of an infinite-layer samarium nickelate film with a Tc of 20 K finds a superfluid density that falls linearly as the temperature rises, consistent with d-wave pairing in the clean limit. The extracted gap is 2.5 meV, a gap-to-Tc ratio of about 3.

recent.h: Spin fluctuations set Tc in electron-doped cuprates
recent.x: Transport measurements on La₂₋ₓCeₓCuO₄ films at 19 dopings isolate a scattering rate that grows linearly with temperature and varies around the Fermi surface, which the authors attribute to spin fluctuations at the antiferromagnetic wavevector. Its strength falls about tenfold as Tc drops from about 25 K to zero and tracks Tc across the doping range, which the authors take as evidence that these fluctuations mediate the pairing.

recent.h: Superconducting-like states and an electrically switchable orbital magnet in six-layer graphene
recent.x: Transport down to 9 mK in rhombohedral six-layer graphene finds two superconducting-like states. In the first, the resistivity drops sharply near 170 mK and survives in-plane fields of about 6 T, far above the Pauli limit of about 0.3 T expected from its Tc. The resistance never fully reaches zero, hence the cautious name. The same device hosts a ferroelectric orbital magnet whose hysteresis can be reversed with an electric field.

recent.h: Oxygen content traces a superconducting half-dome in bilayer nickelate films
recent.x: Compressively strained bilayer nickelate films on SrLaAlO₄, such as La₂PrNi₂O₇₊δ, superconduct best, with onsets above 40 K, at ideal oxygen content. Adding oxygen suppresses superconductivity toward a metal, while removing it drives a granular superconductor–insulator transition and turns the Hall coefficient from negative to positive. Together they trace half of a superconducting dome.

recent.h: Even and odd molecular spin chains couple differently to a superconductor
recent.x: Chains of spin-1 [3]triangulene molecules assembled on a superconducting Au/Nb(110) surface behave as Haldane chains with a free spin at each end. In chains with an odd number of units the end spins combine to a total spin of 1, which binds Yu–Shiba–Rusinov states inside the superconducting gap; in even chains they pair into a spin-0 state that no longer couples to the superconductor. Singlet–triplet excitations measure the exchange between the end spins.

recent.h: A type-I superconductor that breaks time-reversal symmetry: YbSb₂
recent.x: Zero-field muon-spin relaxation on YbSb₂, a type-I superconductor with Tc ≈ 0.95 K and a critical field of about 51 G, picks up a spontaneous internal field of about 0.44 G that appears with superconductivity, the sign of broken time-reversal symmetry. It is the first type-I superconductor reported to do so. A nonunitary triplet state is proposed but not tested.

recent.h: A dark optical cavity raises the Tc of NbSe₂
recent.x: Thin NbSe₂ placed in terahertz split-ring resonators, with no light shone on it, showed a Tc about 0.13 K (roughly 2%) higher in a 12-layer device, and the shift depended on the resonator frequency. The authors present it as evidence for, and a proof-of-principle demonstration of, superconductivity tuned by the vacuum fluctuations of a cavity.

recent.h: Storm 5.0: a 90% range for every prediction
recent.x: Our AI agent proposed six ways to say how sure Storm is, each calibrated by conformal prediction on materials Storm never saw. The winner uses one width on log(1 + Tc), so the range grows with Tc: it held the computed Tc 90% of the time overall and 84% of the time for the tenth with the highest Tc, where a single width for all materials managed only 54%. Half of the ranges are narrower than 1.8 K, so a screen can now look for materials whose whole range is high.

recent.h: Hurricane 2.0: predicting unconventional Tc in two parts
recent.x: Our AI agent’s second round for Hurricane splits the prediction in two: the probability that a compound superconducts at all, times its Tc if it does, with 19 structure types read from the stoichiometry. For compounds whose parent it never saw it is off by 10.3 K, against 12.7 K for Hurricane 1.0 on the same folds, better in all five; on the superconducting entries the error falls from 17.8 K to 12.3 K. The product shrinks the highest predictions, though: Hg-1223, the 133 K record, comes out at 91 K.

recent.h: Storm 4.0: boosted trees and a crystal-graph network together
recent.x: Our AI agent’s second round of crystal-graph networks combined weight averaging, an Allen–Dynes head and Storm’s crystal descriptors. Retrained with two seeds, the network is off by 0.94 K on the computed Tc of materials it never saw, against 0.98 K for the first network and 0.97 K for Storm 1.0. Averaged with Storm 1.0’s trees it reaches 0.90 K, better in all five folds, and calibrated to measured Tc it is off by 1.56 K, against 1.61 K for Storm 3.0.

recent.h: Radar 1.0: an AI-designed router between Storm and Hurricane
recent.x: Radar reads a material’s composition and crystal structure and decides which of our two models to ask. Trained on 5,751 SuperCon entries in 3DSC, it picks the right model 99.5% of the time for parent compounds it never saw, against 98.2% for a composition-only baseline. Left out of training, cuprates still all go to Hurricane, but only 1% of heavy-fermion compounds and a third of the iron-based ones do: a new family needs physics, not only a classifier.

recent.h: Hurricane 1.0: an AI-designed Tc model for unconventional superconductors
recent.x: In this project an AI agent (Claude) proposed nine designs, trained on 2,123 measured Tc values of cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other oxide compounds from 3DSC. The winner adds physics features such as the holes per copper and the d-electron count from charge balance, and cuts the error for compounds whose parent it never saw from 15.0 K to 12.7 K, better in all five folds. A family it has never seen stays out of reach: trained without cuprates, it misses them by 35 K.

recent.h: Storm 3.0: Storm calibrated to measured Tc
recent.x: A small correction model, learned from 298 conventional materials with measured Tc (168 of them superconducting), maps Storm’s DFT-based prediction to experiment. The error against measurement drops from 2.2 K to 1.6 K, below the 2.5 K of the DFT labels themselves, and is lower in all five folds.

recent.h: Neural-network wavefunctions find stripes and d-wave pairing almost tied
recent.x: Neural tensor-network and neural backflow states, run on GPUs for Hubbard lattices of up to 1,024 sites, find that at 1/8 doping a uniform d-wave superconductor, superconducting stripes and non-superconducting stripes lie within about a thousandth of the hopping t in energy, with and without the next-nearest-neighbour hopping of hole-doped cuprates. A preprint, not yet peer reviewed.

recent.h: A dopant–Zhang–Rice-singlet mechanism for the 4a₀ × 2a₀ pattern
recent.x: Matrix-product-state calculations of lightly doped cuprates find that the poorly screened Coulomb interaction between dopants and localized Zhang–Rice singlets favours dipole-like configurations, and that these localized holes create bound states inside the charge-transfer gap. With tunnelling matrix elements included, the bound states take the 4a₀ × 2a₀ shape seen in Ca₂CuO₂Cl₂. A preprint, not yet peer reviewed.

recent.h: A single CuO₂ plane still superconducts
recent.x: A single layer of Bi₂Sr₂CuO₆₊δ (Bi-2201), which holds just one CuO₂ plane, superconducts with an optimal Tc only about 10% below that of thicker crystals. Tuning its oxygen content extends the phase diagram, and between the insulator and the superconductor an anomalous metal appears as the temperature approaches zero.

recent.h: Zhang–Rice singlets and the first Cooper pairs imaged in a cuprate
recent.x: Spectroscopic-imaging scanning tunnelling microscopy of lightly hole-doped Ca₂CuO₂Cl₂ finds that an isolated dopant binds a hole whose in-gap state has the spatial pattern of a localized Zhang–Rice singlet. With more holes, overlapping singlets form rod-shaped “electronic molecules” that gather into plaquettes about four lattice constants across. The first sign of pairing is a U-shaped gap in these molecules, which turns into the sharp V-shaped d-wave gap in extended islands.

recent.h: Eight-leg Hubbard cylinders favour charge order over pairing
recent.x: DMRG (matrix-product-state) calculations of the doped Hubbard model on eight-leg cylinders, at U = 8t and 12t and hole doping 1/12 and 1/8, find a charge-density wave with extremely short-range pairing whenever t′ ≤ 0. For t′ > 0 the result depends on the boundary conditions, so whether pairing or charge order wins in two dimensions is still open.
